During the afternoon of July 3, 1939, 
Mr. H.P. Mills, Publisher of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao 
(2% v% 4), 172 avenue Edward VII, was interviewed 
regarding an insert published in the Hwa Mei Wan Pao 
dated July 1, 1939 announcing the issue of a special 
mumber to commemorate the Loukouchiao Incident and 
inviting contributions of articles etc. He was 
also shown an instruction issued to D.8. Lockwood 
by the Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch). Mr. 
Mills declined to make any comment on the subject, 
merely stating that the arrangements to publish the 
"Special Issue" had been cancelled and that no 
articles or editorial reference to the Loukouchiao 
Incident would be made in the papers under his control. 

Mr. Mills reemphasised that it is his 


antention to co-operate with the Police on every 


possivole occasion.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. __________
S. 5. Special Branch Station,
REPORT    Date July 5 1939.
Subject July 7. Anniversary of the Lukouchiao Incident.

Made by __________ and __________ Forwarded by D. S. Lockwood.

With reference to the endorsement by the
Commissioner of Police on Special Branch report dated
July 3, 1939, I have to report that Mr. Ford of H.B.M.
Consulate-General was interviewed during the morning
of July 5, 1939 when he was asked to communicate with
Mr. Saunders-Yates of the University Press, Ltd., 130,
Ningpo Road, and request him not to publish references to
the incident in the 'Ta Ying Yeh Pao' (大英夜报).

Mr. Ford agreed to the Commissioner's request
and later informed the Special Branch that he had been
in communication with Mr. Saunders-Yates, who was very
reluctant to give an assurance not to print references to
the incident, saying that it was not journalistic ethics
to suppress news of political importance. On being
informed that the editors of all Chinese dailies had
agreed not to publish references to the incident, Mr.
Saunders-Yates promised to comply with the wishes of the
British authorities.

In connection with the registration of British
owned Chinese dailies by the Consulate-General, Mr
Ford intimated that the British authorities intended to
introduce, in the near future, legislation governing
British Registered Chinese dailies which had suspended
publication.

（左侧栏批注及印章）：
Commissioner of Police
Sic.
Thos Robertson
D. C. (Sp. Br.)

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 6 JULY 1939）

During the afternoon of July 3, 1939,
Mr. H.P. Mills, Publisher of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao
(華美晚報), 172 Avenue Edward VII, was interviewed
regarding an insert published in the Hwa Mei Wan Pao
dated July 1, 1939 announcing the issue of a special
number to commemorate the Loukouchiao Incident and
inviting contributions of articles etc. He was
also shown an instruction issued to D.S. Lockwood
by the Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch). Mr.
Mills declined to make any comment on the subject,
merely stating that the arrangements to publish the
"Special Issue" had been cancelled and that no
articles or editorial reference to the Loukouchiao
Incident would be made in the papers under his control.
Mr. Mills reemphasised that it is his
intention to co-operate with the Police on every
possible occasion.

日期 1939年7月3日

事由。 《华美晚报》及《华报》——约谈 H.P. Mills 先生。

制作人及转呈人 D.S. Lockwood

1939年7月3日下午，就《华美晚报》于1939年7月1日刊登的一则启事进行了约谈，该启事宣布将发行纪念卢沟桥事件的特刊，并征集文章等稿件。受访人为《华美晚报》出版人 H.P. Mills 先生，地址为爱德华七世路172号。同时向他出示了副总监（特别科）向 D.S. Lockwood 发出的指令。Mills 先生拒绝对此事发表任何评论，仅表示出版“特刊”的安排已取消，在其控制的报刊中不会刊登任何关于卢沟桥事件的文章或社论提及。Mills 先生再次强调，他有意在一切可能的场合与警方合作。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处总监办公室 1939年7月5日 特别科）

D. C. (特别科)

Special Branch,
July 3, 1939.

D.S. Lockwood.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao.
Proposed Special Issue bearing
on July 7 Anniversary.

Please see Mr. H.P. Mills and request him not
to publish this Special Issue as it is most detrimental
to peace and order and may entail very serious conse-
quences. Further request him to refrain from any
reference to the July 7 anniversary in all papers coming
within his control. You might also remind him of his
assurance to the Council that he would not publish any
inciting or otherwise undesirable matter and his
statement to me personally that "he he does not wish to
go against the police."

〔签名〕
D. C. (Special Branch)

《华美晚报》。
拟出版的涉及七月七日周年纪念的特刊。

请会见 H.P. Mills 先生，并要求他不要出版此特刊，因为这极不利于治安秩序，并可能导致非常严重的后果。进一步要求他在其控制的所有报刊中避免提及七月七日周年纪念。你也可以提醒他此前向工部局作出的保证，即不刊登任何煽动性或其他不良内容，以及他对我个人的陈述：“他不愿与警方作对。”

〔签名〕
D. C. (特别科)

July 2, 1939.                                    Morning Translation.

Eastern Times:

        PRICE OF VEGETABLES INCREASES

            Owing to the report that the transportation of
        vegetables would be controlled by a certain party, a
        general increase in prices was recorded yesterday.
        For instance, the price of white cabbage, which was 4 cents
        a catty on June 30, was increased to 10 cents yesterday.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated July 1:

        SPECIAL JULY 7 PUBLICATION

            To commemorate the anniversary of the July 7
        incident, we have decided to publish a July 7 Special
        Issue on Saturday next week (July 8).    It is hoped that
        readers will contribute as many articles as possible on
        the subject.
                                            The Editor.

《字林西报》：

        蔬菜价格上涨

            由于有消息称某一方将控制蔬菜运输，昨
        日记录到价格普遍上涨。例如，6月30日每斤4分
        的白菜，昨日涨至10分。

1939年7月1日《华美晚报》：

        七月七日特刊

            为纪念七月七日事件周年，我们决定于下
        周六（7月8日）出版七月七日特刊。希望读者能
        就此主题踊跃投稿。
                                            编辑。
